title: Zero was not invented once
summary: MacTutor separates a Babylonian placeholder story from Indian numerals and from the Maya.
body: The MacTutor history of zero, by the St Andrews history-of-mathematics project, says a placeholder zero is not the same as a number that can be calculated with, notes that the Babylonian place-value system went a long time without a full zero, and treats the Indian numeral system and the Maya system as separate developments. The v1 pack does not cover this. A single "who invented zero" question usually hides at least three different inventions. The MacTutor page is a secondary history. It is enough to reject a one-origin story, and not enough to date every inscription.
